# tronc/migrate

Ordered database migrations, applied from inside the app binary.

This is a **separate Go module** from `tronc` itself. It has its own `go.mod`, its own tags, and
its own dependency — [goose](https://github.com/pressly/goose). That separation is the whole
point: `tronc` depends on `chi` and nothing else, deliberately, and a chassis used by ten
services should not put a migration engine in the dependency graph of the ones that have no
database.

## Why it exists

Five of the suite's Go APIs run `gcr.io/distroless/static-debian12`. No shell, no `psql`, no
migration CLI. Dokploy has no pre-deploy hook. So a migration can only be applied by the
application itself — the same constraint that produced `tronc/healthcheck`.

goose also has no `stamp` command ([#431](https://github.com/pressly/goose/issues/431),
[#938](https://github.com/pressly/goose/issues/938),
[PR #954](https://github.com/pressly/goose/pull/954) unmerged), and the raw-SQL workaround needs
a `psql` these containers do not have. `migrate baseline` closes that gap.

## Install

```sh
go get github.com/FacileStudio/tronc/migrate@v0.1.0
```

Note the version query is plain semver even though the git tag is `migrate/v0.1.0` — the
subdirectory lives in the module path, not in the version.

## Use

```go
//go:embed migrations/*.sql
var migrationsFS embed.FS

func run() int {
	// ... open the database ...

	sqlDB, err := db.DB()
	if err != nil {
		return 1
	}

	migrations, err := fs.Sub(migrationsFS, "migrations")
	if err != nil {
		return 1
	}
	migrateConfig := migrate.Config{DB: sqlDB, FS: migrations, Logger: appLogger}

	if handled, err := migrate.Command(ctx, os.Args, migrateConfig); handled {
		if err != nil {
			appLogger.Error("migrate", slog.Any("error", err))
			return 1
		}
		return 0
	}

	if err := migrate.Run(ctx, migrateConfig); err != nil {
		return 1
	}

	// ... serve ...
}
```

`fs.Sub` is not optional: an `embed.FS` preserves the directory it embedded, so passing it raw
means goose looks for migrations at the root and finds none.

## Subcommands

Every image is `ENTRYPOINT`-only, so arguments append to the binary:

```sh
docker run <image> migrate status
docker run <image> migrate version
docker run <image> migrate up
docker run <image> migrate baseline 1
```

| Subcommand | What it does |
|---|---|
| `status` | one line per migration: version, state, applied-at, path. The default. |
| `version` | the current schema version, as a bare number |
| `up` | apply everything pending — the same code path `Run` takes at boot |
| `baseline <n>` | record migrations up to `n` as applied **without running them** |

## Baselining

`baseline` is for a database whose schema already exists but has no migration history — every
Facile database, all built by GORM `AutoMigrate`.

It creates goose's ledger table by asking goose to (never by hand: goose inserts a
`version_id = 0` sentinel row and refuses to operate without it), refuses to run if any
migration is already recorded, checks the version exists, and records every version up to and
including it.

Generate the baseline from **production**, not from the structs — `AutoMigrate` never drops, so
production carries columns the models have forgotten. The recipe, the verification step and the
per-app rollout order are in
`~/.mycelium/memory/standards/migrations.md`, synced to every machine by mycelium.

## Configuration

```go
type Config struct {
	DB     *sql.DB      // required
	FS     fs.FS        // required, rooted at the migrations directory
	Logger *slog.Logger // defaults to slog.Default()
	LockID int64        // defaults to goose's DefaultLockID
}
```

`Run` holds a Postgres session advisory lock for the duration, so two instances starting at once
cannot both migrate. **The pool must allow more than one connection** — the lock pins one, and a
pool capped at one deadlocks against itself.

The provider is never closed: goose's `Close` closes the underlying `*sql.DB`, which belongs to
the caller.

## Requirements

Go 1.25.7 — goose's floor, and higher than `tronc`'s own 1.24. PostgreSQL 10+ for the ledger
table's `GENERATED BY DEFAULT AS IDENTITY`; the suite runs 16.
